subproblem.title: Weighted tangent plane from the tangent plane of a Lusin compact (Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.8(1))
subproblem.statement: Let n, ℓ ≥ 0, U ⊆ ℝ^{n+ℓ} open, and V = v(M, θ) a rectifiable n-varifold in U (contract structure RectifiableVarifold; M = V.carrier, θ = V.mult, μ_V = V.weight). Let K ⊆ M be compact with θ continuous on K, x ∈ K, and P a linear subspace which is the approximate tangent space of K at x (Simon Ch. 3, Def. 1.4). Assume that for every R > 0, μ_V((M ∖ K) ∩ B_{Rλ}(x))/λⁿ → 0 in [0, ∞] as λ ↓ 0 (closed balls). Then P is the approximate tangent space of M with respect to θ at x (Simon Ch. 3, Def. 1.7; Chapter03.HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x P). (Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.8(1).)
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (U : Set (Amb n ℓ)), IsOpen U → ∀ (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U) (K : Set (Amb n ℓ)) (x : Amb n ℓ) (P : Submodule ℝ (Amb n ℓ)), IsCompact K → K ⊆ V.carrier → x ∈ K → ContinuousOn V.mult K → (∀ R : ℝ, 0 < R → Tendsto (fun r : ℝ => V.weight ((V.carrier \ K) ∩ closedBall x (R * r)) / ENNReal.ofReal (r ^ n)) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 0)) → Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n K x P → Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n V.carrier V.mult x P
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the parent proof's step 5e (Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.8(1), with the boundedness from Remark 1.5(3)), with details filled in.

Notation. M := V.carrier, θ := V.mult, μ := V.weight = (Hⁿ⌞M) with density ofReal ∘ θ; ℝ^{n+ℓ} = Amb n ℓ, Hⁿ = μHE[n], B_r(y) closed ball, η_λ := η_{x,λ}, η_{x,λ}(y) = λ^(−1)(y − x) = Chapter03.blowUpMap x λ y; C_c denotes the compactly supported continuous real functions. The contract's structure fields give: M ⊆ U, M is Hⁿ-null-measurable, θ > 0 on M, θ is AE-measurable for Hⁿ⌞M, and θ is Hⁿ-integrable on M ∩ K' for every compact K' ⊆ U. 'T_xK = P' means Chapter03.HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n K x P (finrank P = n and ∫_{η_λ(K)} f dHⁿ → ∫_P f dHⁿ for every f ∈ C_c). W(x, P) means Chapter03.HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x P: finrank P = n and, for every f ∈ C_c, ∫_{η_λ(M)} f(y)θ(x + λy) dHⁿ(y) → θ(x)∫_P f dHⁿ as λ ↓ 0.

Proof.
1. finrank P = n, because T_xK = P.
2. Local integrability. x ∈ K ⊆ M ⊆ U and U is open; fix ρ > 0 with B_ρ(x) ⊆ U. Then θ is Hⁿ-integrable on M ∩ B_ρ(x) and on M ∩ K = K (integrableOn_mult). θ is continuous and positive on the nonempty compact K, so θ ≥ c > 0 on K (IsCompact.exists_isMinOn) and c·Hⁿ(K) ≤ ∫_K θ dHⁿ < ∞; thus Hⁿ(K) < ∞. K is closed, hence Borel.
3. Change of variables (H1). For λ > 0, every function g and every set S ⊆ ℝ^{n+ℓ}:
 ∫_{η_λ(S)} g(y)θ(x + λy) dHⁿ(y) = λ^(−n) ∫_S g(η_λ(z))θ(z) dHⁿ(z),
 because the push-forward of Hⁿ⌞η_λ(S) under the homeomorphism y ↦ x + λy equals λ^(−n)·Hⁿ⌞S (SimonGMT Chapter04.map_inverse_blowUp_carrier, with Chapter04.blowUpHomeomorph), followed by MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map and integral_smul_measure; this identity of Bochner integrals requires no integrability. The same identity holds with θ replaced by the constant 1.
4. Splitting. Fix f ∈ C_c, R > 0 with f = 0 outside B_R(0), M_f := sup|f|, and 0 < λ < ρ/R. The function h_λ(z) := f(η_λ(z))θ(z) vanishes for z ∉ B_{λR}(x), and |h_λ| ≤ M_f·θ on M ∩ B_{λR}(x) ⊆ M ∩ B_ρ(x); h_λ is AE-strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞M; hence h_λ is integrable on M. Writing M as the disjoint union of the Borel set K and M ∖ K, and θ(z) = θ(x) + (θ(z) − θ(x)) on K, step 3 gives
 ∫_{η_λ(M)} f(y)θ(x + λy) dHⁿ(y) = λ^(−n)∫_M h_λ dHⁿ = I_1 + I_2 + I_3, where
 I_1 := θ(x)·λ^(−n)∫_K f(η_λ(z)) dHⁿ(z) = θ(x)∫_{η_λ(K)} f dHⁿ,
 I_2 := λ^(−n)∫_K f(η_λ(z))(θ(z) − θ(x)) dHⁿ(z),
 I_3 := λ^(−n)∫_{M∖K} f(η_λ(z))θ(z) dHⁿ(z);
 all three integrands are integrable (bounded by multiples of 1_K or of θ·1_{M ∩ B_ρ(x)}, using Hⁿ(K) < ∞ and step 2).
5. I_1 → θ(x)∫_P f dHⁿ, by T_xK = P.
6. I_3 → 0. |I_3| ≤ M_f·λ^(−n)∫_{(M∖K) ∩ B_{λR}(x)} θ dHⁿ ≤ M_f·λ^(−n)·μ((M ∖ K) ∩ B_{Rλ}(x)), because ∫_S ofReal ∘ θ d(Hⁿ⌞M) ≤ μ(S) for every set S (withDensity_apply_le) and θ > 0 on M. By hypothesis μ((M ∖ K) ∩ B_{Rλ}(x))/ofReal(λⁿ) → 0 in [0, ∞]; hence it is finite for small λ and its real value tends to 0. So I_3 → 0.
7. I_2 → 0. Let ω(s) := sup{|θ(z) − θ(x)| : z ∈ K ∩ B_s(x)}; ω(s) → 0 as s ↓ 0 because θ restricted to K is continuous at x. Then |I_2| ≤ M_f·ω(λR)·λ^(−n)Hⁿ(K ∩ B_{λR}(x)). The last factor stays bounded (Remark 1.5(3)): λ^(−n)Hⁿ(K ∩ B_{λR}(x)) = Hⁿ(η_λ(K) ∩ B_R(0)) (SimonGMT Chapter04.hausdorff_blowUp_ball) ≤ ∫_{η_λ(K)} g dHⁿ, where g(y) := min{1, max{0, 2 − |y|/R}} is in C_c with 0 ≤ g ≤ 1 and g = 1 on B_R(0); and ∫_{η_λ(K)} g dHⁿ → ∫_P g dHⁿ < ∞ by T_xK = P. Hence the last factor is bounded for small λ and I_2 → 0.
8. By steps 4–7, ∫_{η_λ(M)} f(y)θ(x + λy) dHⁿ(y) → θ(x)∫_P f dHⁿ for every f ∈ C_c; together with step 1 this is W(x, P). ∎
proof_key_steps: finrank P = n; local integrability of θ near x; Hⁿ(K) < ∞ from min θ > 0 on K
Change of variables (H1) via map_inverse_blowUp_carrier, valid for arbitrary sets and integrands
For small λ split the weighted blow-up integral into I_1 + I_2 + I_3 (all integrable)
I_1 → θ(x)∫_P f by T_xK = P
I_3 → 0 by the density hypothesis on μ_V((M ∖ K) ∩ B_{Rλ}(x))
I_2 → 0 by continuity of θ|K at x and the bound λ^(−n)Hⁿ(K ∩ B_{λR}(x)) ≤ ∫_{η(K)} g → ∫_P g

audit.reason: All hypotheses match. Compact positivity and local integrability justify the integrals and finite Hausdorff measure of K. The arbitrary-set transport identity and withDensity inequality accommodate the null-measurable carrier. The three-term decomposition, cutoff bound and density assumption prove the exact weighted tangent predicate.
